content:
maya: quick FYI — new developer hit a blocker in the Ruby quickstart. README still references the old auth helper and the example fails with `undefined method 'refresh!'`.

olivia: ouch. do you have the exact repro steps or paste?

maya: they used `gem 'redwood', '~> 0.3'` per README and ran `bundle exec ruby quickstart.rb`. quickstart.rb calls `Auth::RefreshableToken.new`, which we removed in 0.4.0. macOS + rbenv environment.

sam: thanks, that sounds like a doc/compat issue. we updated the SDK API but forgot sampleapp & README. quick local repro on linux was 30s. can we patch README and add a tiny CI smoke test?

olivia: yes to both. maya can you open a PR swapping the snippet to the new `Redwood::Auth::Client.new(token_refresh: ...)` pattern and bump the example gem version to `>= 0.4.0`? should be small.

maya: on it. will also add a short "Upgrading the Ruby SDK" note in the README explaining the auth surface change.

sam: for the CI smoke, add .github/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml that does `bundle install && bundle exec ruby quickstart.rb` on ubuntu matrix. that should catch regressions.

kevin: please flag for release notes—this will cause confusion for newbies. migration note helpful.

maya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-quickstart/pull/79 — includes README fix + smoke workflow. cc @olivia. :tada:

ci-bot: Build queued for PR #79 — ruby-matrix (2 jobs)

ci-bot: Job ruby-2.7 on ubuntu-latest: PASSED ✅

ci-bot: Job ruby-3.1 on ubuntu-latest: FAILED — bundler error: nokogiri native gem install fails with `nokogiri requires ffi (~> 1.15)`

sam: good catch, CI smoke exposed a separate dependency pain. maya: can you either disable bundler cache or change the example to avoid native gems? for a tiny quickstart using stdlib `net/http` + `json` would be simplest.

maya: switching quickstart to pure stdlib now; updating PR. this removes nokogiri from the dependency graph and keeps the smoke test stable across platforms.

olivia: looks great. after the tweak i'll review & merge. also adding a short blurb in onboarding docs and create a support FAQ note so first-time users don't open tickets for this.

kevin: thanks team. small iteration but great to see smoke CI catching both API drift and platform deps. :clap:
